draft.title: The business cycle and its causes
card: The business cycle is the pattern of ups and downs in real GDP, which is the total output of the economy after removing price changes. Growth speeds up and slows down over time, and it does not follow a fixed timetable.
Expansion and peak
In an expansion, real GDP grows and unemployment tends to fall. The peak is the high point, where growth stops and real GDP turns down.
Contraction and trough
In a contraction, growth slows or real GDP falls and unemployment tends to rise. The trough is the low point, where real GDP turns up again.
Causes

Aggregate demand (AD) is total spending in the economy. Aggregate supply (AS) is total output that firms are willing and able to produce. A rise in AD tends to push the economy into expansion. A fall in AD tends to push it into contraction. A fall in AS can also slow the economy.
draft.remember: Rising AD tends to drive expansion toward a peak. Falling AD tends to drive contraction toward a trough.

a.q: Which description fits the economy at a trough in the business cycle?
opts: Real GDP has stopped falling and is about to rise
Real GDP has stopped rising and is about to fall
Real GDP is growing faster than in the last year
Real GDP is falling faster than in the last year
a.why: A trough is the low point, where a contraction ends and real GDP turns up. The second option describes a peak, which is the high point where growth turns down.
a.clue: A trough is the lowest point of the cycle.

b.q: Households across a country cut their spending sharply, and firms see weaker sales. What is the most likely effect on the business cycle?
opts: The economy moves toward contraction as AD falls
The economy moves toward expansion as AD falls
The economy moves toward contraction as AD rises
The economy moves toward a peak as AS rises
b.why: Less household spending means a fall in AD, which tends to slow real GDP growth and push the economy into contraction. Expansion is tempting but is linked to rising AD, not falling AD.
b.clue: Spending is one part of total demand. Which way does it move?

a.best: Real GDP has stopped falling and is about to rise

b.best: The economy moves toward contraction as AD falls

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'The second option describes a peak', but the options appear in random order. Here the second option is 'Real GDP is falling faster than in the last year', which describes a contraction, not a peak. The peak option is 'Real GDP has stopped rising and is about to fall'. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.
